LESSON: PAPER CRAFT

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Performing and Display
Topic 2.3: Paper Craft
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Paper Craft, part of Performing and Display in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Which items can you make using paper?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify items made using paper craft,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Paper Craft in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. make a paper items using pleating technique,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Paper Craft in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. make paper items using folding technique,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Paper Craft in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. play using the paper items for enjoyment. ● Learners to observe virtual or actual pictures of items made out of paper. Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light. ● Learners to collect varied papers for craft. ● Learners to create paper toys using pleating technique such as animals, fan among others. Learners with manipulation difficulties could type or be supported. ● Learners to narrate about or play with the paper item. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Paper Craft together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: as the learner engages in showcasing, discussing, and playing with their own and

others' paper craft creations, fostering communication skills and collaborative enjoyment of artistic expressions.

• Creativity and Imagination: as the learner makes paper items allows them to explore through transforming simple materials

into playful and visually engaging creations.

• Learning to Learn: as the learner acquires paper crafting skills and techniques, demonstrating an ability to adapt and

continually improve their artistic abilities through exploration and practice.

29

Values:
• Love: is promoted as the learner derives joy from making and playing with paper items reflects a love for the creative

process, fostering a positive attitude toward artistic exploration and expression.

• Unity: is enhanced as the learners collaborate, appreciate diversity in design, and celebrate each other's unique artistic

expressions.

• Responsibility: is promoted as the learner takes responsibility for understanding and implementing pleating and folding

techniques, recognizing the impact of their choices on the overall design and functionality of the paper craft items.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life skills: is promoted as the learner develops self-awareness and self-esteem through display of their work and guiding them

to express their feelings, ideas and emotions.

Link to other learning areas:

• Mathematical Activities: as the learner applies mathematical concepts in pleating and folding such as symmetry and

measurement, providing a cross-disciplinary connection to mathematical activities.

• Environmental Activities: as the learner uses varied papers for craft to support environmental awareness, connecting paper

crafting to broader ecological considerations.

Suggested learning resources:

Sample paper crafts, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, adapted tools and materials such as

looped scissors, heavy gauge papers, scissors with grip, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital devices with

filter keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input devices such as head wand,
